mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month acceleration in personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) above 0.5% quarter-over-quarter signals stronger household demand, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly higher than baseline in quarters where GDPC1 acceleration exceeds 0.5%, or Rank IC < 0.04 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month rise in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which pressure corporate margins and drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline in periods of UNRATE acceleration > 0.3pp, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A 2-month contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below -0.5% signals supply-side stress, which raises input costs and reduces earnings visibility, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline in periods of INDPRO contraction < -0.5%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month rise in the federal funds rate above 4.5% signals a restrictive monetary stance, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline in periods of FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A 2-month decline in real personal income (RSAFS) below -0.5% signals weakening household purchasing power, which reduces demand and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline in periods of RSAFS decline < -0.5%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month acceleration in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above 0.5% signals labor market strength, which boosts consumer spending and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline in periods of PAYEMS acceleration > 0.5%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A 2-month rise in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) above 5% signals a housing market rebound, which increases household wealth and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline in periods of HOUST > 5%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year window.
